content.text:
Yes. I recommend `react-easy-crop` for this flow. It provides drag positioning, zoom, touch gestures, square aspect ratio, and a circular avatar guide. It is TypeScript-ready and mobile-friendly. [Official documentation](https://github.com/ValentinH/react-easy-crop), [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-easy-crop).

Proposed pipeline:

1. Click avatar edit.
2. Select an image.
3. Open a crop modal.
4. Adjust position and zoom with a circular guide.
5. Confirm the crop.
6. Convert the selected area to a square `Blob`/`File` using Canvas.
7. Pass that cropped file into the existing `updateAvatarMutation`.

The library provides crop coordinates; a small local helper performs the actual Canvas export. Browsers do not have a suitable built-in interactive cropper.

One consideration: its documentation warns against scale-based modal opening animations because they can affect cropper measurements. Our modal should use no scale animation, or the cropper should be measured after opening.

This is the most suitable option for the current avatar workflow.
